subject: Finex — throughput & latency follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Singh <lara@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finex — throughput & latency follow-up

Hi Lara —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying asks so we can size a pilot accurately: 

Summary from call
- Primary workload: real-time chat assistance for customer support (short prompts, multi-turn).
- Secondary: end-of-day batch summarization for transcripts.
- Critical SLO: p95 latency for interactive chat; streaming support required for the chat UX.

Clarifying items we need from you (if you can confirm/reply inline that helps):
1) Latency targets: you mentioned p95 ~500ms as a goal — is that for first-byte or full-response? Do you have separate p50/p95 targets?
2) Streaming: chat needs partial-token streaming as the model generates, correct? Any specific client-side timeouts we should be aware of?
3) Request profile: average input tokens and average output tokens per request (and a 95th percentile/max).
4) QPS / concurrency: steady-state QPS you expect during business hours vs peak QPS (e.g., end-of-day or marketing pushes), and typical concurrency (user sessions that will be open simultaneously).
5) Model: do you plan to run an open model we onboarded (you mentioned the "finex-chat-7b" fork) or bring-your-own-model? Any quantization constraints?
6) Compliance: any special logging/retention needs beyond standard audit logs we should factor for Dedicated/Private deployments?

Proposed next steps on our side:
- If you can send the workload CSV (tokens per request, timestamps) we’ll run a throughput-sizing analysis and come back with a recommended baseline (GPU count + autoscale settings) and an expected tokens/sec and QPS target for pilot.
- We can also run a short load test (synthetic) against a staging endpoint to validate p95 latency under steady and peak profiles.

Attached: sample CSV template we discussed.

If it helps, Rafael and I are available tomorrow 10–12 PT to review the file together and lock the pilot dates.

Thanks —
Neha
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: finex_workload_profile_template.csv (CSV stub)
From: Lara Singh <lara@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Omar Khalid <ok@finex.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finex — throughput & latency follow-up

Neha —

Thanks for the clear notes, really helpful. I filled out the CSV and included it as an attachment (finex_workload_profile.csv). Answers inline below: 

1) Latency targets: our product team wants p95 for first meaningful token <= 500ms for chat. Full-response p95 can be up to 1s for longer outputs.
2) Streaming: yes — we rely on token-by-token streaming to update the UI. Client-side timeout is 10s; anything longer we drop.
3) Request profile: average input tokens ~45, average output tokens ~120. 95th percentile output tokens ~350, max 800 in rare cases (long transcripts).
4) QPS / concurrency: steady-state QPS is ~12 QPS (regional US peak hours). Peak events (batch processing / release-days) can spike to ~80 QPS for ~5–15 minutes. Typical concurrent sessions ~40, peak concurrent ~200.
5) Model: we plan to use the finex-chat-7b (open fork) quantized to 8-bit. We can test with the unquantized variant if helpful.
6) Compliance: standard audit logs are fine; need 90-day retention for request metadata.

Procurement note: we're targeting a pilot contract in August. Deal id in our system is FINEX-PO-4891 if you need to reference.

Attached: finex_workload_profile.csv

Cheers,
Lara
Head of Product, Finex

FYI — Lara sent back the workload CSV and the answers. Highlights that affect sizing: steady 12 QPS, short inputs (45 tokens) but longer outputs (avg 120, up to 350 p95), streaming required, p95 first-token target 500ms, peak bursts to ~80 QPS and peak concurrency ~200 for short windows. They want 90-day audit retention.

Rafael / Marissa — can you take a first pass at a recommended pilot config and an estimated GPU count (we'll include autoscale/burst plan)? I'm thinking we propose a dedicated pilot with autoscaling to handle the 80 QPS bursts and an initial steady-state capacity sized for 12 QPS.

Proposed immediate deliverables: 
- Rafael: throughput estimate (tokens/sec per GPU) and recommended #GPUs for steady vs peak.
- Marissa: billing/contracting note for an August pilot (duration 6 weeks) and whether we need an SLA exception for streaming p95.

Attaching our recommendation draft (redwood_throughput_recommendation_v1.pdf) — it's a draft with baseline assumptions.

Thanks,
Neha

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Lara Singh <lara@finex.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finex — throughput & latency follow-up

Great notes all — thanks Lara and Neha. Based on the profile and assumptions (finex-chat-7b @ 8-bit, streaming required, avg output 120 tokens, p95 output 350 tokens) here's an initial sizing estimate and test plan: 

Key math (rounded):
- Steady: 12 QPS * (45 in + 120 out) ~= 12 * 165 tokens = 1,980 tokens/sec steady-state.
- Peak burst: 80 QPS * 165 tokens ~= 13,200 tokens/sec (for 5–15 minute windows).

GPU throughput assumptions (conservative, post-quantization, with continuous batching + KV cache for multi-turn):
- Single GPU effective sustained tokens/sec ~= 1,800 tokens/sec (depends on sequence lengths and batching; real-world could be 1.5–2.2k).
- Streaming adds little per-token overhead when we use incremental generation hooks but does reduce maximum batching efficiency by ~10–15%. We baked that into the 1.8k estimate.

Sizing recommendation:
- Steady capacity: 2 GPUs (2 * 1,800 = 3,600 tokens/sec) — covers steady 1,980 tokens/sec with headroom and allows room for background jobs and autoscale cooldowns.
- Peak capacity (target for safe headroom during 80 QPS bursts): 8 GPUs (8 * 1,800 = 14,400 tokens/sec).
- Autoscale policy: maintain 2 GPUs steady; allow rapid scale to 8 GPUs on sustained QPS > 20 for >30s; allow burst to 10 GPUs for extreme spikes (safety).

Test plan:
1) Synthetic load test (we run): replay finex_workload_profile.csv against staging endpoint with real token distribution and streaming enabled — measure p50/p95 first-token and full-response latencies.
2) Live pilot: provision Dedicated pilot with throttled capacity; run 1-week pilot with observed load to validate production assumptions and tune batching/kv cache TTLs.

SLO note: target p95 first-token <= 500ms — with the above sizing we expect to meet this under steady and moderate bursts. For sustained 80 QPS we hit p95 close to target; actual will depend on exact batching characteristics. We'll instrument and run the test to validate and tune (e.g., increase batch size TTLs or add ephemeral burst capacity).

Next actions:
- Neha: confirm you want us to schedule the synthetic test (Rafael & infra team will run) — propose Thu 2027-07-29 09:00 PT.
- Lara: if that time works, please confirm. We'll need an API key for staging and the CSV you attached (we have it).
- Marissa: please draft the pilot contracting note for 6 weeks (include autoscale billbacks) and confirm any SLA exception process for streaming windows.

I'll attach a short lab-run checklist after the test. Happy to jump on a quick call if anyone wants to walk through the assumptions.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
